recommendations.text: For patients presenting with acute chest pain, a 12-lead ECG should be obtained and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact to evaluate for STEMI (Class I, Level of Evidence B).
For patients with suspected ACS, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) should be measured at presentation and serially to diagnose or exclude myocardial injury (Class I, Level of Evidence A).
Aspirin 162-325 mg loading dose should be administered to all patients with suspected ACS unless contraindicated (Class I, Level of Evidence A).
For STEMI patients, primary PCI is the recommended reperfusion strategy when it can be performed within 120 minutes of first medical contact. The goal is door-to-balloon time of 90 minutes or less.

In patients with inferior STEMI, right-sided ECG leads (particularly V4R) should be obtained to evaluate for right ventricular involvement. Nitrates and other preload-reducing agents are contraindicated in RV infarction as they may cause severe hypotension.
For NSTEMI patients, an early invasive strategy (within 24 hours) is recommended for patients with high-risk features including elevated troponin, dynamic ST changes, or GRACE score > 140.
P2Y12 inhibitor therapy (clopidogrel, ticagrelor, or prasugrel) should be initiated in addition to aspirin in patients with ACS undergoing PCI (Class I, Level of Evidence A).
Anticoagulation therapy (unfractionated heparin, enoxaparin, or bivalirudin) should be administered to patients with ACS (Class I, Level of Evidence A).

key_sections.stemi_management: ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) requires emergent reperfusion therapy. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the preferred strategy when performed by experienced operators within 120 minutes of first medical contact. Fibrinolytic therapy should be considered when PCI cannot be performed within the recommended timeframe. Adjunctive therapy includes aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors, anticoagulation, and beta-blockers.
key_sections.nstemi_management: Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) management includes dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin plus P2Y12 inhibitor), anticoagulation, and risk stratification. An early invasive strategy is recommended for high-risk patients. Conservative strategy may be appropriate for low-risk patients.
key_sections.rv_infarction: Right ventricular infarction complicates approximately 30-50% of inferior STEMIs. Diagnosis requires right-sided ECG leads (V4R). Management focuses on volume loading to maintain RV preload. Nitrates, diuretics, and other preload-reducing agents are strictly contraindicated as they may cause catastrophic hypotension. Dobutamine may be needed for persistent hypotension after volume loading.
